title: Patch: an imagined opponent whose reply reaches its step cap still makes its attacks and ends its turn, where a five-use Activate now hides a lethal
thread:
**Issue #4810 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #4810: Patch: an imagined opponent whose reply reaches its step cap still makes its attacks and ends its turn, where a five-use Activate now hides a lethal
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What happens

The opponent model's reply (`simulate_reply_with`, `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`) runs at most `AI_REPLY.max_steps` (12) steps. When it reaches the cap it returns `Some(current)` with the opponent still on turn (`reply.rs:911`, `:999`), and `replied_score` scores that state as a finished reply. Each step does one thing, in the order known play, visible Activate, Deft trial, attack (`reply.rs:936-959`), so what the cap cuts is the attacks.

Stinkyscape #66 Miner v5 ("Activate 5: Gain a random Stinkyscape Resource", no cost) is enough: each use gains a Resource, the Resource is a new instance and so not among the hidden cards, and `known_play` plays it on the next step. Five mines and five plays are ten of the twelve steps.

Board: the AI at 12 with no Unit; the opponent has three 4/4s and a Miner. Without the Miner the reply kills the AI. With it (seed `audit-reply-miner-7`, where the Resources are heals and 1-damage pings), the reply makes two attacks and then the loop runs out: the state handed back has no result, the opponent is still on turn 10, the AI is at 2 and one 4/4 has not swung. The line is scored as survived.

In a fuzz of 12 random-policy games, 5 of 154 replies stopped mid-turn this way, all with a Miner in play.

### What should happen

`reply.rs:887`: the reply runs "until the seat's next main phase or prompt, or game end". `crates/ai/src/config.rs` describes `max_steps` as covering "plays, attacks, prompt answers and the closing endTurn". `crates/ai/README.md` has the reply play the Activates it can see "then its attacks". A capped reply should still make its attacks and close the turn, or the cut should be reported so the line is not scored as answered.

### How to reproduce

Fails on `main` (3a83bd7): `a_five_use_activate_does_not_crowd_the_opponents_lethal_attacks_out_of_the_reply` in [`crates/ai/tests/audit_reply.rs` at bf24a52](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/bf24a52273bd5c0e7d6f9c740b28a8d7cb7f2b3e/crates/ai/tests/audit_reply.rs) (branch `claude/vigilant-mayer-pmyrhr`).

```rust
// handed_over_on(seed, p1, p2): a turn-9 scenario with p1 active, then p1's End turn through `reduce`.
#[test]
fn a_five_use_activate_does_not_crowd_the_opponents_lethal_attacks_out_of_the_reply() {
    let reply = |field: Value| {
        let state = handed_over_on("audit-reply-miner-7", json!({ "health": 12 }), json!({ "field": field }));
        let counter = create_node_counter(600, None);
        simulate_reply(&state, AI, &counter, &hidden_card_ids(&state, AI), Prices::NONE).expect("a reply")
    };
    let plain = reply(json!(["core-008", "core-008", "core-008"]));
    assert_eq!(plain.result.map(|result| result.winner), Some(Winner::from(HUMAN)));
    let mined = reply(json!(["core-008", "core-008", "core-008", "stinkyscape-066"]));
    let unswung = active_units_of(&mined, HUMAN).into_iter()
        .filter(|unit| unit.def_id == "core-008" && !unit.exertion.attacked).count();
    assert_eq!(mined.result.map(|result| result.winner), Some(Winner::from(HUMAN)),
        "beside a Miner v5 the reply stopped with the opponent still on turn: active {:?}, turn {}, \
         the AI at {}, {unswung} of the 4/4s unswung",
        mined.active, mined.turn, mined.players[AI].hero.health);
}
```

Output today: `beside a Miner v5 the reply stopped with the opponent still on turn: active P2, turn 10, the AI at 2, 1 of the 4/4s unswung`.

The test depends on its seed because the Resources are random; on other seeds the board still reaches lethal (fewer plays beat standing still). Pin the scene so a balance patch cannot move it (a stand-in with a free five-use Activate, if the testkit allows one).

### Where

The AI: `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` (`simulate_reply_with`'s loop and what it returns at the cap).

### Version or commit

`main` at 3a83bd7.

### Notes for the fix

- Cap the steps that are not attacks apart from the attacks (for example, stop trying known plays and Activates once a share of `max_steps` is spent), and when the cap is reached with the opponent still on turn, close the turn with `EndTurn` so the line is scored at the seat's next decision, as every other reply is.
- Any new number is a named constant in `AI_REPLY` (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
- `max_steps` appears in no test, in neither the README nor SPEC §9, and in no ruling, so nothing pins the cut; this is a decision the spec does not make, so it takes a ruling note in this issue's block.
- A change here moves what the reply plays on boards with many Activates, so fixed-seed AI games can move. `training/improve.md` says how a change to the AI's play is screened; say in the pull request what was measured.
- Not among the findings of the AI audit tracker #4787.

Found by an audit of the AI crate; the reproduction was run and the code path read before filing.
````
